```{r}
#Where do people get their news
mediatypes <- read.csv("Comp 112 Data - Sheet1 copy.csv")
head(mediatypes)

#How often do people use social media to get their news (Pew Research Center)
smrates <- read.csv("smrates - Sheet1 copy.csv")
head(smrates)


#What % of people use social media to get their news by demographic (Pew Research Center)
demrates <- read.csv("demrates - Sheet1 copy.csv")
head(demrates)
```

```{r}

library(tidyverse)

demrates |>
  summary(demrates)

```
::: {.callout-note title="Reflection"}

From the summary, we can see that the Facebook has the highest overall median, meaning the most uses for political information. Serving as the overall platform for political information on social media. 

:::


```{r}

demrates |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Facebook:Instagram,
    names_to = "Platform",
    values_to = "Percentage"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Platform, y = Percentage)) +
  geom_col()
```

::: {.callout-note title="Reflection"}

This graph allows us to easily compare the how much people use certain platforms. From the graph, people tend to use Fackbook more commonly 

:::


```{r}

mediatypes |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = TV:None,
    names_to = "News_Source",
    values_to = "Percentage"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = Percentage, color = News_Source)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point()

```
